cards.explanation: The answer is “You are the Christ.” Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, says, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” No hedging and no "well, some folks say." After a whole round of what other people think, he just says it plain, friends.
The answer is True. Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah!” Simon son of Jonah is Peter. Jesus answers a big confession with a blessing, not a lecture, friends.

The answer is Jesus' Father in heaven. Jesus says, “For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.” So Peter's answer didn't come from his own figuring or from a crowd. I think that makes it a pretty special thing to say out loud.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “…I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.” The church He builds stays standing, and the gates of Hades don't win, friends.

The answer is that it will be loosed in heaven. Jesus says, “Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.” The two halves match up: bind with bound, loose with loosed. That's Jesus talking to Peter, right after promising him the keys.

The answer is False. Jesus “…admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ.” He gives them the opposite of a megaphone, friends. The text doesn't say why, so I'll leave that open too.

The answer is that He will be raised to life. Jesus says He must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed, “…and on the third day be raised to life.” The hard news and the good news come in the same sentence. Listen to the whole sentence, bakers.

The answer is True. “Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.” He says, “Far be it from You, Lord!” and “This shall never happen to You!” Right before that, Jesus had told His disciples He must suffer and be killed (Matthew 16:21). I think Peter's heart was in a big hurry, but the text just tells us what he said.

The word is “men.” Jesus says, “…you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” It's a direct line to Peter, friends. It comes right after “Get behind Me, Satan!” so Jesus is plain with him here.

The answer is his cross. Jesus says, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.” Three things in a row, friends: deny himself, take up his cross, follow. Jesus says this to His disciples after telling them what's ahead.

The answer is that he will lose it, and yes, it sounds backwards. Jesus says, “For whoever wants to save his life will lose it…” Holding on tight ends up costing the thing you were gripping, bakers. Then He turns it around in the second half of the verse.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “…whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.” So the one who loses it for His sake finds it, friends. The other half of the verse is the one about losing.

The answer is True. Jesus asks, “What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul?” He asks it as a question, and the answer is left for us to think about, bakers. Then He asks one more.

The answer is that He will repay each one for what he has done. Jesus says the Son of Man “…will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.” Notice that it's each one, friends. I'm not here to tell you when, only to keep the ovens ready (Matthew 24:36).

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.” So some of them will see it, friends. He says it with “Truly I tell you…” and I don't try to say more than the verse does.
